name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visual: Mine AI website/product DESIGNS (the look), taste-learn from Eitan's picks.

name: Easel
text: I’ll pull Eitan’s 3 latest design picks from the shared drive (`/designs/eitan-picks/2024-06/`), open them in Figma (files: `pick-01-miner-light.fig`, `pick-02-miner-dark.fig`, `pick-03-miner-mono.fig`), and export 4K PNGs for side-by-side moodboard comparison—then drop them into `/room/visual/moodboards/eitan-2024-06/` so the lead can declare the aesthetic direction.

name: Squint
text: Squint here—hold up. You’re assuming Eitan’s picks are *current* and *representative* of the latest design direction, but the folder’s dated June 2024. Where’s the evidence these aren’t stale? And exporting static PNGs for a moodboard ignores the interactive, dynamic nature of Mine AI’s product—how do we know the visual language holds up in motion or user flow? Show me the delta between these picks and the *actual* product’s UX before we lock in.
